name: LE-7A
tagline: Japan's staged-combustion hydrogen core, two decades of H-II service
description: The LE-7A is the engine that gave Japan a fully indigenous heavy-lift capability. Developed by Mitsubishi Heavy Industries for JAXA, it runs a staged-combustion cycle on LOX and LH2 — the thermodynamic approach that extracts maximum efficiency from hydrogen propellant — and first flew on H-IIA in August 2001 as a refined successor to the original LE-7. The redesign addressed turbopump issues that had caused early H-II failures, and the LE-7A went on to anchor H-IIA and H-IIB's operational careers through 2024, launching Japan's HTV cargo ships to the International Space Station and the JAXA-ISRO radar satellite ALOS series.
best_known_for: Japan's staged-combustion hydrogen core — powered H-IIA/H-IIB
